about:
Experienced Microsoft enterprise infrastructure design and solutions consultant with emphasis on Windows Server, Microsoft Exchange, Active Directory, SharePoint Infrastructure, Office 365 and Microsoft Azure. Worked on several small, medium and large scale projects. 

Served as a developer, engineer, architect, team lead and project manager across various engagements.

experience.position: Assistant Director | Messaging Foundation Services | Global Infrastructure Services

experience.description: Usman is a Principal Consultant for Intellinet Corporation, working on Platform Strategy and Cloud Delivery for several customers. Area of specialization includes; Exchange Server 2003/2007/2010/2013, Windows Server Active Directory 2003/2008/2012, Office 365 & Microsoft Azure.

Usman led all project efforts to rebuild a mid-size SharePoint 2007 farm to the latest SharePoint 2013 release in a stable, highly available environment for the fourth largest school district in Georgia. Utilized custom developed .NET solutions and the Metalogix Content Matrix product to perform a content based migration. Managed a team of 4 .NET developers, 1 business analyst and 2 graphic designers.

Usman established the Microsoft Infrastructure Practice. Developed material and served as a trainer on Microsoft Exchange 2003 - 2010. Performed deployments on cross-forests, data center consolidations, organization consolidations, organization disjunctions and directory synchronization engagements.

Usman performed the Exchange migration for several customers including; Tapco Underwriters, deploying multiple Mailbox servers, Hub servers, Edge servers, Client Access Servers and Threat Management Gateway for secure OWA on VMware ESXi across multiple A.D sites.

Performed the phase II build of the Bank Of America bankruptcy charts and graphs managed by NBS. The rebuilding of the bankruptcy graphs and charts were performed using SSRS, C#, Dundas Charts and SQL Server in a fast-paced agile project for the forecasting of various chapters of bankruptcy handled by NBS clients, primarily Bank of America. Managed a team of 2 .NET developers.

Usman delivered the project of migrating the messaging environment for the entire CCSD school district from Exchange 2003 to Exchange 2010 with plans for High Availability (HA) and Disaster Recovery (DR). Implemented the Blackberry Enterprise Server (BES) upgrade from  4.1 to 5.0.1.

Usman was responsible for the Microsoft SharePoint mid-level sized farm pilot deployment across the entire company, spanning multiple geographic locations. Trained, mentored and provided strategic guidance to junior members of the IT team and identified power users.

Usman worked as a SharePoint developer to implement custom site request with 2-stage approval workflow and an automatic site provisioning application featuring custom site templates, rules-based template selection, automatic enforcement of security and navigation policy, and automatic maintenance of farm-wide sites list used for governance.

Usman worked with UCMC internal technical engineers to provide guidance on a new Microsoft Office SharePoint Server (MOSS) 2007 for internal administration staff and student collaboration. Collaborated with business users; produced governance plan, policies and procedures, roles and responsibilities, information architecture, global site navigation, and search strategy.

Usman worked on the SharePoint collaboration platform (Atlas) rebuild on Windows SharePoint Services 3.0. Developed InfoPath forms workflow application used across three IT groups to automate gathering information and approvals for the marketing offer implementation process.

Usman performed research on utilizing SAML (Secure Assertion Markup Language) for mobile Identity Management. Applied various concepts of cryptography; Symmetric-Key cryptography, Public/Private Key cryptography, Secure algorithms, AES, RSA, Digital Signature generation/verification for signing SAML.

headline: Senior Technology Consultant at EY
about:
I graduated in May 2019 from the Kelley School of Business at Indiana University majoring in Information Systems, with a specialization in Information Management, and minoring in Sports Marketing and Management.

I began my career with Ernst & Young in October 2019 as an Advisory Staff Member in the Technology Advisory Program based out of EY’s Chicago office.

My internship experiences with Walmart and Republic Airways have helped me to hone my organization and leadership skills, presented me with challenging opportunities to expand my critical thinking abilities, and enabled me grow professionally prior to beginning my full-time career.

While at Indiana University, I had the opportunity to be on the executive committee for the Business World of Sports Club.  This experience taught me how to effectively lead students in workshops and case competitions and gave me the opportunity to communicate and present information to large groups of people on a regular basis.  I also held a part-time job at McAlister’s Deli which helped me develop stronger time-management skills by balancing time between work and school.

I am a hardworking, responsible individual who has a passion for helping other people succeed. I am a gifted motivator who is able to challenge those I am around to achieve their highest potential. I believe people are most successful in achieving their goals when working through collaboration with others and through effective leadership. Throughout my time at IU and in my internships, I have learned that teamwork is vital to accomplishing any goal, no matter how big or small.  I strive to draw upon my values of faith and family, and all of my past experiences, to help drive me to be successful in everything I do.

projects.title: Claim-i-fly
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
projects.description:
Developed a decentralised web application which facilitates buying/selling of flight insurance and claiming it digitally with ether (ETH) being the mode of payment.

Designed a smart contract using Solidity on Remix IDE, running on the Ethereum platform, that can successfully validate and verify transactions.

Used Ganache as my personal Ethereum blockchain network, Metamask to keep a track of the digital transactions, SendGrid Mail API to automatically e-mail insurance details to the insurance owner, and CoinMarket API to convert SGD to ETH based on the market price.

projects.title: SUTDCoin
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
projects.description:
Worked in a team of 4 to design and implement a cryptocurrency called SUTDCoin using concepts from the Blockchain course at SUTD.

Designed the entire blockchain network for SUTDcoin to allow students to transact using SUTDCoins, and allow miners to mine the blocks with successful transactions onto the blockchain network by demonstrating Proof-Of-Work (PoW).

Leveraged on Bitcoin’s Proof-of-Work concept to help facilitate the design of SUTDCoin’s blockchain network.

projects.title: WhatNext?
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
projects.description:
Worked in a team of 3 to develop a text prediction machine learning model which suggests users with words to complete a sentence based on their texting behaviour by assigning probabilities to the words and tags at their respective position in a sentence.

Used Hidden Markov Model (HMM) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) concepts to develop the model for suggesting the appropriate word with the highest probabilistic prediction score based on the previous word(s) and the overall sentiment of the sentence.

Achieved an overall prediction accuracy of 97% during the testing phase, by optimising the weights of our model during training and validation.

projects.title: Master-Analysts
projects.description:
Performed in-depth financial analysis on Mastercard’s stock (NYSE: MA) and recommended a BUY decision.

Leveraged extensively on Bloomberg Terminal to analyse and model quantitative data about Mastercard and its competitors.

Analysed quantitative parameters and metrics such as Earnings Estimates, P/E ratio, Dividend Payout, Free Cash Flow, Intrinsic Value - to name a few - along with qualitative parameters such as global news, macroeconomic and microeconomic information before confirming the BUY decision.

projects.title: Bit Combat
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
projects.description:
Worked in a team of 4 to create a shooting game in which two players compete against each other by moving around a 7x7 LED matrix and shooting bullets at each other using arcade buttons.

Used concepts from the beta architecture of a von Neumann machine extensively to develop this game on a Field  Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) Board (Mojo V3) that utilises a 16-bit ALU we developed using Lucid on Mojo IDE.

Bit Combat was chosen as the course’s best project by the faculty and students, based on voting administered by the Office of Student Administration of SUTD, and it will be showcased to public during future outreach events at SUTD.

projects.title: DigitalQ
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
projects.description:
Led a team of 6 to develop an Android application called DigitalQ, with an aim to digitalise the queue system for stalls in food courts around Singapore.

DigitalQ allows merchants to create, configure and manage queues for their stalls, while customers can view, join, and manage these queues at their own convenience. The app notifies the customer when his/her turn is approaching.

Used Java, Object-Oriented Programming, Android Development concepts extensively on Android Studio; used Google Firebase as our app’s cloud database for the back-end.

projects.title: GetTheFit
projects.description:
Selected by the Entrepreneurship Centre at SUTD to attend the European Innovation Academy- a startup accelerator and entrepreneurship program- in Turin, Italy.

Developer an android application for a B2B startup ‘GetTheFit’- an online marketplace for women to trade clothing.

projects.title: Leaf-Me-Alone

Used Kivy, based on Python, to create the app interface; Google Firebase to store and retrieve moisture levels, light  intensity and live image at a recurring frequency; coded the Raspberry-Pi for multiple sensors and camera used.

projects.title: EyeSense

publications.title: Taxing Marijuana and the Road to Reparations: Comparing the Colorado and Illinois Cannabis Markets
publications.publishedAt: Duke Journal of Economics - Duke Journal of Phylosophy, Politics, and Economics · Jun 2, 2020
publications.description: Although still prohibited at the federal level, cannabis can now be found on the shelves of recreational dispensaries across thirty-three U.S states. This thesis examines the development of this legal market from both historical and empirical perspectives. Using a new data set, it estimates the determinants of cannabis sales and tax revenues in the Colorado market and analyzes the incidence of a single tax increase. The results, which suggest that legal cannabis behaves like a luxury good, are used to analyze the potential for cannabis-funded reparations programs in Illinois, which recently approved recreational sales of cannabis.

headline: Global Location Investment, Credits and Incentives Services
about:
I am a multifaceted and versatile Manager in EY's Indirect Tax practice based in Minneapolis, Minnesota. My practice focuses primarily on advising multinational clients on location investment strategy to include financial analysis, federal, state, and local tax credits, and discretionary incentives. I have also developed a deep expertise in advising clients on Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) tax credits to build their financial justification to advance Environment, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.

Previous experience include corporate finance, corporate middle market banking and credit analysis, and local/state economic development responsibilities with public and private sector organizations. I have also developed expertise in global trade through previous experience as the grantee of Foreign-trade Zone 119.

featured.title: Career Breaks and Returning to a Very New Working World
featured.subtitle: Brandon Brown on LinkedIn

slides.title: Career Breaks and Returning to a Very New Working World
slides.subtitle: Brandon Brown on LinkedIn
slides.description: It’s crazy to think it’s been nearly five years since I left my career, packed all of my belongings in a backpack and started traveling the world. But as that adventure has come to an end and I’ve started my new position with EY this week, I’ve found myself particularly reflective and anxious. It’s been quite the adjustment; not only am I returning to the working world after such a long career break but also one in which, everything is entirely virtual. I’ve adapted quickly though and I think more than anything I’m just incredibly grateful for such a promising opportunity, given the circumstances with the pandemic and the job market. I’ve had fellow travelers returning from a similar career break ask me for advice as they navigate their own job searches. Certainly its a unique situation but I thought it might be helpful to share my experience and advice with a larger audience. I’ve also talked with numerous people during my interviewing process as well as new and former colleagues that were curious to know more about my story and travels, so if anything maybe you’ll simply find it interesting. Take Ownership of the Experience Often when I’ve talked to others, they’re unsure of how to address their career break and discuss it in a meaningful way. There’s a fear that it might be interpreted as a whim or lack of regard for their career but that’s almost never the case. My career has always been very important to me but I equally value my personal life and traveling the world and living abroad was one of my greatest life dreams. While it was one of the most difficult decisions I’ve ever made, I knew looking at the big picture that this was the most opportune time. I was young and healthy, financially able, and with enough professional experience to skillfully market myself upon a return. So I decided to take a pause in my career. It was a strategic and thoroughly planned move, right at the end of a project assignment, and I left on great terms with my old company and client. During this time I traveled and lived in Asia, Australia, New Zealand, South America, and Europe, working various casual jobs, volunteering and documenting the experience in a travel blog. I motorbiked across Vietnam, trekked in the Himalayas, skydived in New Zealand, and cycled the Death Road in Bolivia. They’re memories of a lifetime and something I take great pride in. These were honestly the best years of my life and I have absolutely no regrets. It’s really critical to project this confidence when discussing your career break and own it. Translate the Experience to Relevant Work Value and Be Honest You weren’t working, so what were you doing? That’s the question that often causes the most anxiety and fear. The purpose of my career break was to see the world and travel, not to advance my professional goals or have some great epiphany. That’s acceptable and I’m entirely honest when I discuss my experience. If you gained any professional skills, that’s great! You should highlight those. But don’t think that’s all that matters. Perhaps more than the adventure and travels, the experience speaks to my personality and the attributes that make me a natural at consulting - a constant sense of curiosity, learning and critical thinking, an ability to adapt quickly to new surroundings, able communication, and a propensity for developing close relationships. Those soft, transferable skills are invaluable to employers and they often come hand in hand with travelers who are instantly and regularly forced to adjust to new customs and cultures, communicate without language, make new friends, and survive and navigate in a new foreign country. More than anything, I accomplished one of my great life dreams and that is admirable in itself. Nearly every person that I’ve spoke to shares my dream of traveling the world but not many ever take the leap. Now that I’ve done it, I have an immense feeling of freedom; there’s no longer that lingering desire or regret hanging over my head and I can fully invest in my career, building on my previous professional experience but also with the renewed energy and passion of a new hire. Positioning yourself in this way, makes it easier to translate your value to employers. Utilize Your Network and Get Your Head Back in the Game Regardless of a career break, networking should be an essential part of any job hunt and always used as a starting point. One study even suggests that nearly 85% of jobs are hired through networking. While this number maybe inflated, I will say that I personally fit within the statistic having obtained my job offer through a referral from a former colleague. You should reach out to close former colleagues to casually let them know you’re looking for work. And before applying for any job, always search your network to see if you have any connections at that company and if so, reach out to them. More often I reached out to my connections simply to ask for advice and get a feel for the current trends in my industry and the job market. This was informative but more importantly it guided me on how I should be marketing myself. I asked friends to review all of my resumes and cover letters, which were redrafted countless times. Whether it’s job referrals, advice, editing, or just venting, your network is your greatest asset. Getting that first interview is the hardest part, then it’s all up to you. You can anticipate probably 95% of the questions that are going to be asked so you really have no excuse not to be prepared. I spent hours upon hours prepping for interviews and made certain that I had my career break explanation perfected in a one minute elevator pitch. It was definitely a bit scary and daunting when I initially started my job search process but it’s important to stay positive and not lose focus. Maintaining your mental health is essential and I always did my best to eat healthy, exercise, and regularly talk with friends. Anytime I got particularly discouraged I also found it comforting to go through old travel photos. It was a helpful reminder of just how fortunate I was and gave me the necessary motivation to continue. You just have to keep applying, and applying, and applying. Things will eventually work out and you’ll land the right opportunity. Strangely, it was only as I started writing this post that I was reminded of an article I wrote about a year ago, Millennials — Redefining Work and Driving Meaningful Change. I discussed the importance of work-life balance, the shift to remote and flexible work arrangements, company culture, employee wellness, social responsibility, and continual learning and how our generation could more rapidly influence positive change in the workplace. Little did I know that a global pandemic would force us to instantly address many of these issues and re-evaluate our purpose and the way we work. These times have been difficult and challenging and while I’m hopeful that some of these positive impacts will stick in the post-pandemic world, there will certainly always be a need to push for improvements in the workplace. I would jokingly argue that there maybe no better person to advocate for this change than an idealistic Millennial just returning from a five year career break and backpacking adventure around the world. It seems all the more fitting then that I’m starting my journey with EY, a firm whose purpose is to Build a Better Working World.

I am an eclectic reader, enjoys thought-provoking conversations, and have a passion for large scale social impact. I believe building modern institutions (or recasting existing ones) with an appropriate mandate is an essential and sustainable instrument for making this change. 

Over the last 14+ years of my career, I have worked for more than a decade with Governments (the largest institution for driving social transformation) in various capacities: as a Fellow embedded within a State Dept, as a Service provider, as a Partner, as a Funder, and now as a Trusted Advisor, to drive large scale projects.  

The top five works so far for which I am proud of are:

1)	Serving as a trusted advisor to an Indian Ministry for few recently launched large-scale initiatives in environment sector. 
 
2)	Serving as a trusted Advisor to a UK based one of the largest philanthropic institutions for implementing State Action Plan for Climate Change in partnership with an Indian State Govt.

3)	Facilitated 750+ Million Euros of climate friendly investments in India as a staff member of a bilateral financing agency operating in India in partnership with the Dept. of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Govt. of India.  

4)	Anchored large scale climate co-benefiting projects in water and natural resources management sectors in several States of India (Assam, Rajasthan, Chandigarh, Himachal, Kerala) as well as with the Indian Urban Ministry of India in partnership with top bureaucrats of India. 

5)	Led the 2nd edition of the National Swachh Survekshan (the annual ranking of cities on Sanitation) and Certification of Cities/Towns on Open Defecation Free (ODF) status on behalf of Govt. of India. 

I am one of the authors of the TERI-USAID report - State of Urban Water and Sanitation in India (released in Oct 2017). I feel fortunate to have been the recipient of the Univ. of Chicago Harris School of Public Policy-IIC fellowship (2015-16), the Piramal Fellowship for Sustainable Business (2011-13) and a Gold Medalist during my Sustainability Master’s programme at TERI (2013-15). I have also been a part of the awakening Yatra led by the Hon'ble MP Shashank Mani Tripathi (earlier Tata Jagriti Yatra in 2009) and attended the UChicago Delhi Centre led Anubhav Lecture Series (2018). 

I take pride in supporting young professionals who connects with me and wish to navigate their career in social impact sector by providing few hours of my time every month.

headline: Assurance Managing Director at Ernst and Young LLP
about:
Annie Kolman is a CPA that has worked in the Assurance practice at Ernst & Young serving large, global organizations. Her professional experiences include the following: 

• Has worked internationally and has coordinated and managed Fortune 500 international audits. 

• Has rotational experience at Ernst & Young's Transaction Advisory Services Gorup serving both private equity and public companies with completion of financial due diligence projects for buy and sell side engagements. 

• Has SOX experience, including implementing,coordinating, and managing testing strategy and workplans for SOX 404 work utilizing Auditing Standard 5 (AS5)

• Has experience with complex inventory concepts (i.e. LIFO, lower of cost or market, mark to market), auditing derivatives, goodwill impairment, etc. and IFRS to US GAAP conversions from working on a large client’s 20-F filing overseas. 

In addition to Annie's client service responsibilities, she was previously the executive sponsor over the Central Region's Data Processing team helping oversee the data transformation group.  Annie has previously served as an Executive Sponsor of the Exceptional EY Internship Program in the Chicago office and also served as the US-Central Digital Implementation Lead helping engagement teams expand their digital footprint within their audits in addition to her client-serving responsibilities.  She has also been an active member of the the Pan-Asian Professional Network (PAPN) Affinity Group at EY formerly serving as the Group's Lead in Chicago as well as formerly serving as the PAPN group's Events Committee Chairperson, a former member of the EY Chicago People Advisory Committee, and formally serving as the co-chair of the staff/senior Networking Sub-Committee for the Professional Women's Network at EY.  She is also actively involved with the recruiting and retention efforts at EY both on and off campuses.

Annie was the winner of the 2014 Illinois CPA Society and AICPA's Women to Watch Award in the Emerging Leader category.

Annie also serves on the Illinois CPA Society's Diversity Advisory Council.

headline: Financial Services Business Transformation Consultant at EY, Miami University Farmer School of Business Alumna
about:
In May of 2024, I graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Business with a major in Finance at Miami University's Farmer School of Business. During my time in college, I served as Vice President of Finance in my sorority, Kappa Kappa Gamma, and I was actively involved in Delta Sigma Pi Professional Business Fraternity as well as Women in Finance Business Organization.

As a well-rounded student on campus, I was able to perfect my interpersonal skills both in and out of the classroom, such as written and oral communication, public speaking, critical thinking, teamwork, leadership, and problem solving skills. My strong work ethic complemented all of these and landed me a spot on Miami’s President's or Dean’s List for almost every semester that I was enrolled. 

Aside from this, my classes polished my quantitative skills in Excel, Access, Tableau, Microsoft PowerBI, Oracle SQL, and R. Additionally, I excelled in courses that taught me financial literacy, calculus, upper-level business statistics, micro and macroeconomics, financial and managerial accounting, business communication, business law, and the desire to embrace ambiguity in our volatile business world. 

Also during my time, I have been engaged in various case competitions: The Key Bank Client Challenge Project, Abercrombie & Fitch’s Freshman Forum, a Liquid IV Marketing Campaign Competition, and Union Home Mortgage's Summer Intern Case. In each these rich experiences, my teams and I were faced with current obstacles related to each business, and I got to play an innovative role that allowed me to show off my leadership skills. We used both primary and secondary data to come to conclusions as to where we needed to improve sales revenues and increase retainment rates for Gen Z customers. In the end, my team came up with possible solutions and presented them to top executives to be considered for implementation. Each of these client’s cases provided me with valuable experiences that uncovered my ability to be a team leader, and taught me how to analyze data in a real world setting and use it to enhance my problem solving. 

My campus involvement, rigorous coursework, invaluable experiences, and strong work ethic have tremendously aided in my growth as a young business professional. I am elated at the opportunities ahead of me to gain further knowledge and skills through my first full-time job as a Financial Business Consultant at Ernst & Young in Chicago.

headline: Audit Partner at EY
about:
I am an Audit Partner in our Chicago office. With over twelve years of experience in a public accounting firm, I have provided Audit, Assurance, and Advisory services to several of our firm’s global priority accounts in the life sciences, manufacturing, distribution, and consumer products industries. In my role, I am responsible for maintaining global client relationships, advising on accounting matters, and managing multiple engagement teams.
 
Previously, I was a Senior Consultant in our National Advisory Services practice, specializing in Finance Performance Improvement. Specifically, I focused on finance transformations, including operational restructuring and shared services, as well as post-merger integration, including legal entity rationalization and consolidation. I also consulted with clients on financial statement close processes, operational and control process improvements, and risk management.
 
Before, and after, joining the firm’s Advisory practice, I have overseen several of our firm’s global priority accounts in the life sciences, manufacturing, distribution, and consumer products industries within Audit and Assurance services. In this capacity, I was responsible for managing a variety of engagement teams and projects; specifically, my experiences have included first-year initial audits, acquisitions and purchase accounting, SEC comment letters, and initial public offerings.
 
I am passionate about recruiting talent to the firm. I currently support our campus recruiting efforts at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign as the Assurance Service Line Lead, a national priority school for the firm and my alma mater.

volunteering.description:
College MAP, EY's signature volunteer program in education, was launched in 2009. It is a long-term, team-mentoring program focused on empowering students in underserved high schools so that they can gain access to college and succeed in higher education. College MAP matches EY volunteer mentors (of all levels, backgrounds and service lines) with groups of local 11th and 12th graders. The team-mentoring model allows EY professionals to share volunteer responsibilities, encouraging personal work/life balance. During interactive monthly workshops, mentors and students explore various topics, which aim to develop each student's: 

Awareness - exposing students to different college opportunities and the lifelong benefits of higher education.

Financial literacy - demystifying the process of applying for financial aid and paying for college.

Persistence - providing personal support and coaching on the life skills that will help a student stay in and complete a four-year degree.

projects.title: Libya and the Human Smuggling market. How things have changed.
projects.description:
This study consider how the market structure of the human smuggling business has changed in Libya after the state collapse in 2011. 
The proposed project proves that when the State is present, few firms are in charge of this business and moreover they operate with a quantity constraint. When the State is no longer present instead, there is no authority that is controlling this process or is really weak, due to that firms produce more and the market concentrate. Once the general results of the model have been defined, the comparative statics will be taken out to the data in order to see if the empirics are in line with what the theoretical model predicts. Finally using a difference-in-difference identification strategy, where Libya is the treatment group and Algeria, Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia the control one it will be determined if the number of fatalities by departure point has increased in a way that is systematically correlated with the state collapse.

topSkills: Finance Transformation • Operating Model Design • Finance Strategy
about: Finance Transformation Leader with 8 years advising CFOs and Senior Executives on diagnostics, operating-model design, and execution of multi-workstream value-creation programs. Deep expertise across Source-to-Pay (STP), Order-to-Cash (OTC), Record-to-Report (RTR), Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), GBS/SSC, ERP-enabled transformation, automation pathways, close acceleration, and control remediation. Known for converting complex Finance challenges into execution-ready roadmaps and delivering $10M–$200M+ in efficiency, scalability, and enterprise-level savings.

experience.position: Manager | Finance Transformation & Operating Model Design | EY
experience.description:
As Manager within EY’s Finance Transformation practice, I lead a global, multi-tower transformation for a $20B consumer-products company, steering a ~$120M value-creation initiative across STP, OTC, and RTR. I oversee end-to-end diagnostics, operating-model design, and the development of execution-ready value-creation roadmaps that integrate ROI, sequencing, KPIs, and investment requirements.

I own the enterprise business case and value-realization model—quantifying productivity, automation uplift, labor arbitrage, working-capital impact, and close-cycle acceleration—and translate these insights into CFO-level decision frameworks. I architect the future-state finance operating platform (service delivery, org structure, governance, and global process standards) while orchestrating alignment across Procurement, IT, HR, Commercial, and regional leadership.

As a strategic advisor to the CFO, Controller, and Global Process Owners, I guide governance sign-off, post-transaction stabilization, and transition readiness for global shared services and technology enablement. My role blends strategic design with hands-on execution, integrating multiple workstreams into a single, cohesive transformation narrative.

experience.position: Senior Consultant | Finance Transformation & Global Business Services | EY
experience.description:
As a Senior Consultant in EY’s Finance Transformation & GBS practice, I led multi-tower workstreams across operating-model redesign, global shared services stand-ups, and ERP-enabled process modernization for Fortune 500 and mid-market clients. I operated as a de facto manager on several engagements—guiding global delivery teams, shaping executive narratives, and translating diagnostics into execution-ready transformation plans.

I led the stand-up of a 60-person Finance Managed Services delivery team in Buenos Aires for a ~$30B Power & Utilities enterprise, overseeing knowledge transfer, workflow design, SLAs/KPIs, and readiness for scaled service delivery. I also delivered significant shared-services transformations, including the launch of a 60-person Finance SSC in Latin America and the transition of R2R/Cash Application to a 70-person center in Bangalore—each driving ~30% cost reduction, stronger controls, and more predictable month-end execution.

Beyond delivery centers, I played a pivotal role in designing a new Global Business Services function for a Fortune 200 CPG company (~$26B), developing the operating model, governance, roles & responsibilities, service catalog, and end-to-end GBS toolkit adopted by senior leadership. I facilitated leadership workshops, managed cross-workstream alignment, and served as a trusted partner to future GBS leaders.

Across these programs, I advised Finance executives on diagnostics, future-state process design, automation and workflow enablement, workforce strategy, and value-creation roadmaps spanning STP, OTC, RTR, and FP&A. My work blended structured problem solving, global team leadership, and hands-on program management—consistently delivering measurable efficiency, enhanced governance, and scalable Finance operations.

As a Consultant in EY’s Finance Transformation practice, I operated as the PMO backbone for major Finance and ERP transformations—driving governance routines, risk and dependency management, integrated planning, and C-suite reporting. I supported SAP S/4HANA Central Finance for a $12B science company and led day-to-day PMO coordination for a 150+ person, multi-vendor global ERP program—ensuring alignment across workstreams, stabilizing delivery, and shaping early operating-model and value-realization decisions.

As a Business Development Intern at Ascensus, I supported strategy and client-facing efforts for one of the nation’s largest administrators of state-sponsored 529 plans. I contributed market and financial analysis on plan performance, fees, and competitive positioning, helping senior leaders assess growth opportunities and partnership strategy. I also developed client materials used in meetings with state treasurers and program managers and assisted with RFP coordination, pipeline tracking, and cross-functional collaboration across Marketing and Finance. The experience strengthened my early foundation in financial analysis, structured communication, and stakeholder support.

about:
As a member of the EY Americas Office of Public Policy, I lead strategic engagement programs targeting key internal and external stakeholders and develop and coordinate messaging for our Americas executives on public policy developments with implications for EY and the markets. I also manage various stakeholder relationships and collaborations designed to advance EY programs and public policy priorities.

I bring a wealth of strategic engagement and public affairs expertise on issues relating to financial institutions, investors, boards, and capital markets, as well as strong background in journalism, marketing, and digital and traditional communications. In 2021, I earned a certificate in Christian Ministry and Theology from Campbellsville University. I also became a TRACOM® Certified SOCIAL STYLE® & Versatility Instructor. In 2023, I contributed to an international best-selling publication - Awakening the Power Within: Stories of Transformation & Triumph.

I am passionate about continuous learning, writing, travel, and the power of effective teams. The title I am most proud of is mom. Contact: erica.e.hurtt@ey.com ‪or ericahurtt@yahoo.com

publications.title: Life according to the GOAT: 10 lessons to live by
publications.description: In Life According to the GOAT, Hurtt shares life lessons from observing goats, drawing parallels between goat behavior and human behavior. Clever, curious, affectionate, and funny, her goats serve as a beacon of optimism and have given her a more positive outlook on the world. Through countless hours of work and play, Hurtt developed a better understanding of goats, and her insights offer readers perspectives on how to live a life defined by wonder and resilience. Imparting 10 goat-approved lessons to live by, Hurtt presents an unconventional approach to personal growth. For anyone looking for encouragement or inspiration, this book is a guiding light.

publications.title: Awakening the Power Within: Inspiring Stories of Transformation and Triump
publications.description:
Join us on a journey of self-discovery, soul healing, and resilience as these brave women share the unique personal transformation they each experienced when they decided to go deep within themselves and harness their power to navigate and overcome some of life’s greatest challenges. They share in celebration of these life-changing shifts that are sure to inspire hope, motivate, and enlighten you to see the possibility of creating positive change in your own life.

Experience the roller coaster of emotions these women endured through their stories of learning the value of listening to their heart, breaking out of the box of societal expectations, and healing from within so they could start living their lives as the creator of their own happiness.

These are everyday women speaking to other everyday women like you to light your way toward awakening your own power within as we rise together to ignite this beautiful ripple effect of self-empowerment, courage, and hope around the globe.

The powerful insights and profound wisdom that come through in every story will resonate deeply with you, as will the invaluable tips and practices that will catalyze your positive transformation. This is a MUST read, as these stories will touch your Soul and speak to you on a level much deeper than words.

headline: EY Principal | Digital Engineering and Manufacturing Transformation
about:
As uncertainty reigns supreme in the US and around the globe, organizations are needing to make pointed decisions on how to expand margin and maximize organic growth through their operations.  I help manufacturing companies achieve this through the appropriate balance of process refinement, digital enablement and physical automation that allows agility and efficiency within their factories.  Leveraging my background in Engineering and nearly 25 years working for and with manufacturers, I bring an outside-in perspective to support inside-out viewpoints to build and execute a manufacturing revitalization strategy.

I've supported companies in nearly every sector but specialize in industrial products, chemicals, automotive and aerospace.  I currently live in the Chicago suburbs.

experience.position: Sr. Manager, Digital Operations Performance Improvement
experience.description:
I work with global manufacturers to help them transform their facilities into leaner, more productive and digitally-enabled operations.  Whether it's designing a new operating strategy, implementing digital tools like mobility solutions or coaching and training the work force, my role is to drive speed to value in order to optimize performance.

As a Sr. Manager, I design programs, develop teams and implement programs that help our clients tackle their most challenging issues within their operations.  With specializations in Lean manufacturing, people enablement, operational excellence and digital manufacturing, I enjoy working with all levels of an organization.

As part of EY's Advisory Performance Improvement practice, I worked with clients and EY leaders to identify and deliver projects.  Selected engagements included a comprehensive review of Operational Risk Management principles and practices across a North American Energy Company, a yield and production optimization program for a US-based industrialized products manufacturer, an asset, maintenance and turnaround program for a US-based chemicals company focused on improving performance of the facilities they operate.  I also acted as a global leader in Operational Excellence and North American lead for Asset Integrity and Reliability.

With responsibility for new business development in the US, I worked closely with the Senior Leaders and Key Influencers of potential clients to understand their current state and perceived needs in order to build a customized solution to help them accomplish their objectives and meet their goals.

Included in my role were new marketing efforts, client relationship development and opportunity identification.  I have an office in Chicago and help clients unlock value through custom consulting solutions in Operations Risk Management, Operational Excellence, Learning & Development and Sustainable Growth.

In this role I was responsible for leading teams of consultants to deliver a variety of consulting services.  My work was focused with large, multi-national oil companies, most notably with off-shore drilling contractors.  The projects I managed spanned multiple continents including N. America, S. America, Europe and Africa as well as the Middle East.

In this role I was responsible for implementing operational improvements through onsite assessment and delivery services with clients in packaging, hospitality, food manufacturing, electronics, agriculture, transportation and industrial chemicals.

In this role I was responsible for managing cost and productivity improvement projects at the DuPont LaPorte Poly Vinyl Alcohol facility.  Using traditional DMAIC and Lean practices, I led multiple projects to reduce variable cost and release unforseen capacity.

In this role I oversaw the production of the DuPont LaPorte Poly Vinyl Alcohol facitility and managed all aspects of production including process optimization, cost, quality, safety, product wheel and transportation logistics.

In this role I managed a team of mechanics and electricians at the DuPont Chattanooga Engineering Polymers facility.  I was responsible for maintenance schedule, cost, productivity, overtime management, personnel development / turnover and systems optimization.  This included managing all facility turnarounds.

In this role I was responsible for maintaining the DuPont Chattanooga High Temperature Nylon process.  Responsibilities included process optimization, quality management and six sigma Green Belt actvities.

headline: People Consultant at EY
about:
I am driven to create change by building genuine relationships within any workplace. My goal is to be an emotional caregiver in the workforce and impact those around me.

I started my undergraduate journey as a psychology major wanting to integrate my knowledge with the psychology and business realm. With my minors in both business and sociology, I am also interested in organizational behavior. I flourish in environments where I am able to learn and apply my skills. I have had experiences in the tech, semiconductor, automotive, education, music, and pharmaceutical industries (previously at Tesla and Samsung). I hope with my experiences in learning & development and talent acquisition, I am able to bring a breadth of new insights. I am a strong advocate of diversity and inclusion, and I am open to any workplace that provides a safe space for all individuals. 

Highly skilled HR Specialist with extensive experience in learning and development, instructional design, talent acquisition, and project management. Committed to fostering a positive work environment and maximizing employee productivity. 

As a staff consultant at EY, I utilize my expertise in supporting clients and develop a high-performing workforce. With my background in consulting and HR, my hope is to one day be a leader for the APAC region.

headline: CRISC | IT Audit | Digital Regulatory Compliance | SOX | Tech Risk | Data Analytics
about:
I am an experienced risk consulting professional with a passion for innovative digital solutions and emerging technologies.

In my previous job as a Manager in the Business Consulting practice of SGV & Co. (Philippine affiliate of Big 4 accounting firm Ernst & Young) where I had worked for eight years, I managed projects in internal audit, US SOX controls audit, IT general controls review, internal controls review, COSO internal controls framework, data privacy assessment, enterprise risk management, SSC process integration, and compliance audit.

I served clients from the banking and securities, transportation, media and entertainment, hospitality, gaming, automotive, insurance, online retail, shared services, professional services, telecommunications, healthcare, consumer products, mining, education, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, and food services industries.

experience.description:
Major engagements:
1. SOX 404 Controls Testing:
I was part of multiple cross-border teams that delivered multi-year SOX audit projects for:
the North American subsidiary of an international automotive company, an American Fortune 100 corporation that is also the world’s largest construction equipment manufacturer, an American casino and hotel company, and an American food company. headline: Audit Manager at EY | Greater Chicago Area | Eli Broad College of Business | MS in Accounting
about:
As an enthusiastic auditing professional from Taiwan, who pursued my education and started my career in US, and now continue my profession in Stockholm, Sweden, my diverse international background has equipped me with an open mindset to appreciate different values and made me proud of who I truly am. After arriving in the United States in 2018, I acquired my Master of Science in Accounting from Michigan State University – Eli Broad College of Business in May 2020, with the cohort recognition as Mr. International Accountant and Mr. Most Outgoing person.

Upon graduation, I received my license as a U.S Certified Public Accountant (Michigan) and started my career in US as an auditor with Ernst & Young, one of the largest professional services firms in the world. Fast forward to the beginning of 2022, I accomplished a transfer and continued my profession with Ernst & Young in a brand-new country, brand-new continent, as a senior auditor. My engagements are heavily involved with US Capital Automotive and Manufacturing industry clients across both Public and Private Sector, following guidance of US GAAP.

Outside of the occupational role, below are the events I have been involved with at EY:

-	Unity Diversity and Inclusive Network
-	EY Training and Facilitation 
-	EY Digital Badge 
-	EY Connect Day
-	Campus Student Mentoring
-	Campus Recruiting

My passion in leveraging my rigorous academic knowledge and professional attributes, including leadership, teamwork, and communication skills, enables me to contribute value towards making a better working world.

experience.position: Senior Audit Associate - US Capital Market
experience.description:
EY auditors serve the public interest by delivering high-quality audits with independence, integrity and professional skepticism.

My role as a senior auditor at Ernst and Young includes: 

•	Perform strategic planning to determine in scope audit procedures for both primary team and 30 component teams and identify risk of material misstatement to address risks and ensure GAAP compliance.

•	Adapt and execute substantive audit procedures, such as Journal Entry testing, overall analytics review and data analytics programs, etc., on various financial statement accounts, including significant risk and higher risk estimate areas.

•	Test the design and operation of internal controls over various business processes, including FSCP, order to cash, restructuring, pension and tax, etc., to ensure data integrity and evaluate control effectiveness.

•	Coordinate both FAIT and Tax teams with planning and ICFR procedures to deliver higher integrated audit quality, by involving them with EDAP and Step 1, 2, 3 meeting following guidance of Project Insight and Project Concord.  

•	Facilitate and mentor staffs / interns on EY global audit methodology, technology, account or SCOT specific audit procedures, and general accounting knowledge to maintain continuous audit quality at all levels.

•	Leverage and integrate GDS into onshore team to increase profit margin, assign and monitor GDS work progress for the timely delivery, and provide coaching to improve overall workpaper quality.

EY is one of the largest professional services firms in the world that provides consulting, assurance, tax and transaction services that help solve our client’s toughest challenges and build a better working world for all.

My professional skills have been greatly enhanced since my start with the firm last year and my accomplishments include:

•	Develop strong interpersonal skills through discussion with client personnel pertaining to their internal control procedures and treatment of major account balances and through organizing team building events within the engagements

•	Maintain open communication with client contacts and the engagement team to ensure that quality and efficiency are continued throughout the engagements

headline: Attorney specializing in HR mergers & acquisitions, executive compensation and benefits
about: An ambitious, diligent, and detail orientated problem solver. My professional work experience prior to and during law school includes six years of experience in the legal field. Following law school, my work has focused on assisting companies navigate HR mergers and acquisitions. Projects have focused on both pre-close and post-close work from a buy and sell side. From a pre-close perspective, I help companies evaluate HR risk and cost considerations so that HR deal drivers can be considered in purchase price and planning. Post-close I have assisted companies ensure that deal drivers are upheld by assisting with projects related compensation and benefits, providing PMO support and acting as a subject matter expert.

honorsAndAwards.description:
In previous years, the college has selected one outstanding student to receive its highest honor, the Ted Bauer Leadership Award, named for Charles T. “Ted” Bauer. This year, with $30,000 funding from Willis Group, the college celebrated six students with the award, including four undergraduates and two graduate students. "Blythe Perez, pre-business major: Perez recently earned the highest spot by a Bauer student in the 2012 CME Group Commodity Training Challenge and is making the most of her time in the college and the university. As a UH cheerleader, Perez works to inspire her fellow Cougars on and off the field, pushing herself to become a leader within the Finance Association as an officer and within the Bauer Leadership Council as a member"

honorsAndAwards.title: CME Open Outcry Competition at Bauer- 3rd place overall
honorsAndAwards.description:
Organized by the student organization and hosted March 31 in Melcher Hall, the open outcry competition required students to test their ability to buy and sell oil contracts using the traditional trading terminology and fast-paced hand signals.

Bauer students made up more than half of the top 10, with Blythe Perez taking the third prize of $500, Sameed Gagai taking fifth place, respectively, and Alyson Quintana, Ben Barr, Pete Watson and Lateef Frierson rounding out the top 10.

The competition is a simulation of the “open outcry” method that commodity traders employ when executing orders. Participants learn about the how markets move due to the supply and demand of a simulated economy, trading crude oil and gas futures. To determine the winners, judges will assess the students’ use of fast-paced hand signals and shouting traditional trading terminology while listening and reacting to the changes in market.

projects.title: Trinity Valley Food (Brakebush INC)
projects.description:
Trinity Valley is a family owned business that was acquired by Brakebush Inc. in 2013. It is a wholesale distributor of poultry products whose main sales channels are food restaurant chains, food service distributors and further processing operators. It has production lines for cutting and marinating boneless chicken.

Itelligence Inc. came into play in June 2013 as a key player to incorporate Trinity Valley into the information technology landscape of Brakebush. One of the key components of that landscape was SAP. The Itelligence team and I as its FICO lead rolled out successfully SAP in December 2013. The components implemented were: Production Planning, Materials Management with lean warehouse management, Sales and Distribution, FI and Controlling. 

It was a project that came with the template of Trinity Valley Parent company and it had some complexity in the areas of production planning and product costing. The conversion of Microsoft based costing sheets into SAP based cost component structure was a challenge along with teaching the concepts of product costing to the TVF people. In addition to that, the lean warehouse implementation took some weeks to be assimilated.

projects.title: PrimeSource LLC
projects.description:
PrimeSource Building Products is a wholesale distributor owned 100% by Itochu building product, a public company traded in the Tokyo stockmarket. It is one of the biggest distributors of building materials in North America with products such as anchor bolts, builders hardware, blades, screws, roofing products, fences, strapping, etc,,, 37 distribution centers in the USA and 6 in Canada.

Itelligence Inc started this project back in June 2011 as a part of a huge overhaul in the IT department. The project was envisaged to put 4 distribution centers and corporate in SAP in the first wave as of April 2012. It involved consultants from logistics areas like materials management and sales and distribution, Vistex for the rebates and discount agreements with vendors and customers, Finance and Controlling with special compliance to IFRS standards and US GAAP, FSCM,  EDI implementation for sales orders and payments, BOBJ as a business intelligence repository of financial and logistic reports and Business planning and Consolidation. In addition to that, there was a team involved in change management tasks such as training and documentation.

The big Challenge was to standardize the business scenarios in order to put them in SAP and integrate seamlessly different apps within its landscape: Vistex, EDI, BOBJ and BPC. 

In FI-CO area the most demanding task was to reconcile profitability analysis with financial reports and stabilize the collection of cash due to the fact we had to work with two live systems until all distribution centers were in SAP.

projects.title: Alliance Laundry systems
projects.description:
ALS is a leading designer, manufacturer and marketer in North America of commercial laundry equipment used in laundromats, multi-housing laundries and on-premise laundries. Well known brand names are Speed Queen, Uni Mac, Huebsch, IPSO and Cissell.

It was a full cycle implementation of core SAP modules including MM, SD, PP and FICO along with business warehouse for sales and financial reporting. 

Main challenges of the project was to implement production planning and product costing due to the depth of its bill of material (more than 10 levels of sub-assemblies) that needed to be redesigned by using phantom materials.  With than being said, we went live successfully in April 2011.

publications.description: This chapter, which appeared in a recent international anthology on consumer protection law, is a broad overview of United States consumer protection law and enforcement. It focuses on the utterly decentralized nature of consumer protection law in the U.S. and the combined roles of federal, state, local, and private law in deterring, detecting, and punishing deceptive and unfair conduct that injures consumers. It further summarizes federal, state, local, and private litigation options to obtain damages, restitution, and injunctive relief for consumers on an individual and class action basis. It ends with a partial list of consumer associations and other private non-profit group working in the consumer protection field.

headline: Senior Manager, Assurance EY FSO
about:
After graduating from the University of Calgary with a Bachelor of Commerce in accounting, I began full time employment with Ernst & Young Calgary and obtained my CPA, CA after passing the 2015 UFE. After completing a 16 month assignment to the EY Tokyo office (EY ShinNihon LLC) in the Financial Services sector (FSO), I returned to Calgary as a manager in our assurance practice.  I subsequently returned to the Tokyo FSO practice in 2020 and have continued my career as an assurance senior manager in FSO. Currently, I am on rotation from EY Tokyo FSO to EY Chicago FSO, leading teams on large PCAOB-IA audits.

I am always looking for unique opportunities to utilize my skills as a business leader, team player and innovator. I have had many opportunities to work with international businesses to gain a better understanding of how businesses operate around the world and has provided me new skills to grow as a leader. My core experiences are in financial reporting under IFRS standards with some experience in USGAAP reporting. I also have extensive SOX reporting experience with my work in Internal Controls Over Financial Reporting (ICFR). Aside from my current focus in the financial services sector and insurance, I also have several years of audit experience in a variety of industries including: telecommunications and media, oilfield waste management, consumer products and manufacturing, construction and power and utilities. I also have several years of experience in global audits and group-wide reporting. In addition to my core assurance profession, I am an active DE&I ambassador at EY, I continually uphold and promote well-being practices and am always advocating for innovative teaming.

Although most of my client facing work requires my focus on IFRS and ICFR standards, I have had work experiences in the private sector; reporting under other frameworks as well. headline: Associate Director at EY
about:
Experienced Finance & Accounting Manager with 16+ year track record of achievement in executing and enhancing planning and reporting procedure; leading process and system change initiatives; advancing performance optimizing strategy; and delivering successful results for large, public and private Big Four (EY, KPMG) and Fortune 100 (Kraft Foods, Ford Motor Co) entities.

•	Financial Planning & Analysis:   Extensive experience managing all aspects of the budgeting and planning process. Analytically strong, excellent communicator recognized for bringing focused insight and perspective to the assessment and discussion.

•	Customer Orientation:   Outgoing style and adept at tailoring approach to effectively reach an audience and support an individual objective. Proven success navigating multiple responsibilities and competing interests across all organizational levels.

•	Project/Change Management:   Demonstrated ability to thrive in dynamic, fast-paced environments. Ushered in 2 separate enterprise system conversions and led numerous other integration and process development/optimization endeavors to successful conclusion.

experience.description:

•	Collaborate cross-functionally (EM, WFP, Ops, Talent, Quality, Markets & BD) to effectively analyze, implement and monitor plan/forecast commitments and strategic objectives of the firm, region and service line.

•	Align with finance and client facing leaders to reconcile the oftentimes-competing interests and objectives of the business, our people and internal & external customers.

•	Support the continued evolution of EY’s internal finance function by enabling transformation initiatives around Mercury, One EY, MBA support model, web-based rolling forecast, Growth & Investment Planning and centralized PDF Center.

•	Promoted to FP&A Manager supporting the U.S. Audit Practice and 3 distinct Business Units generating $325M+ of annual revenue with 1K FTEs.

•	Acted as primary Finance Business Advisor to BU Partners and stakeholders in developing and executing forward-looking plans to meet fiscal and KPI commitments, enhance efficiencies, improve resource utilization and optimize portfolio performance.

•	Developed automated tools to streamline processes and enhance interaction in reporting and communication, e.g. leadership dashboards and goal-aligned forecast frameworks.

•	Led annual plan and periodic forecasting, analysis and variance recommendations to achieve cross-functional results and implement risk mitigation strategies with functional and regional leaders.

•	Supported the U.S. Audit Practice with progressive growth in responsibilities culminating in promotion to FP&A Manager; applied prior relevant experience to successfully facilitate firm-wide conversion to SAP.

•	Received “Executive Recognition Award” for specialized Aircraft Lease Initiative which resulted in $1.3M savings.

•  Selected for Corporate Internship Program during two consecutive summers, and worked in all facets of retail management over four year period, including sales, inventory management, credit and pricing.

featured.title: Invisible tech, visible trust: Leading AI with emotional intelligence
featured.subtitle: Kurt Solarte on LinkedIn

slides.title: Invisible tech, visible trust: Leading AI with emotional intelligence
slides.subtitle: Kurt Solarte on LinkedIn
slides.description: Trust in AI won’t come from capability – it will come from clarity and empathy. One in 10 people globally now socialise with AI – chatting with a virtual friend, confiding in a chatbot or engaging with a digital companion. But in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand, the mood is different. We’re more sceptical, more wary, more anxious. According to the EY AI Sentiment Index, only 37% of Australians and 28% of New Zealanders believe the benefits of AI outweigh the negatives. Whether it’s misleading information, security risks or social engineering, Australians and New Zealanders are more concerned than their global counterparts. They also think AI is making us less intelligent (AU 53%, NZ 42%). When we asked people to share their experiences with AI, words like “dehumanising,” “invasive,” and “annoying” were common. “We as humans are becoming less and less useful,” one person noted. What we have is not a technology problem. It’s an emotional problem. What we can’t see, we don’t trust Most people don’t realise how deeply AI is woven into our daily lives – from the voice that answers your questions, to the filters that sort your inbox, to the chatbot that handles your customer service query. It’s everywhere, but it’s often operating behind the scenes. And that’s the problem. When technology is hidden, it feels unaccountable. What we can’t see, we don’t trust. Globally, excitement for AI is soaring – 84% of respondents in India and 83% in China say they are excited about the future of AI and what it means for them. Here, only 38% of Australians and 33% of New Zealanders share that optimism. Despite the hesitation, AI is being embedded into every corner of business. Whether people are ready or not, it’s happening. That’s why we need leaders who bring emotional intelligence to the table – leaders who help people adapt, not just expect them to keep up. And just as importantly, we need AI systems that are transparent and referenceable. People need to understand how decisions are made, where outputs come from, and what data is driving them. Trust isn’t built on complexity – it’s built on clarity. If we want AI to be accepted in our part of the world, it must be explainable, visible, and human-led. Leadership in the AI era Leaders helping their teams adapt will need technical understanding and strategic insight. They’ll also need human relationship skills and change management abilities. They must build their technical literacy to oversee AI implementation while maintaining high EQ to support the transformation. This is human-centred leadership. Since 2022, EY teams have been working in collaboration with the with the Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, to define six characteristics of human-centred leadership – and they apply here. 1. Lead with empathy: Listen without judgment. Host open Q&A sessions where employees can voice concerns about AI. Acknowledge what you know and what you don’t. 2. Inspire with vision: Use stories, not statistics, to explain how AI creates value. Make your vision clear, relatable and empowering. 3. Care with insight: Understand that experiences with AI vary. Show people that their concerns are heard. 4. Empower with autonomy: Set clear rules, roles and responsibilities for AI adoption. Show people the efficiency opportunities and communicate how you will and will not use AI. Give teams the freedom to experiment without fear of failure. 5. Build with integrity: Balance innovation with ethical responsibility. Establish clear guidelines and ensure AI use is transparent and accountable. 6. Collaborate with clarity: Make AI a shared journey. Encourage teams to share ideas, co-create solutions and build confidence together. The world is embracing AI. Leaders in Australia and New Zealand must close the trust gap – not with technology, but with empathy.

slides.title: Return to Office: a Change? or More of the Same?
slides.subtitle: Kurt Solarte on LinkedIn
slides.description: As a leader in our business, I am grappling with the what/how/when of “return to office” for our teams. While I have poured over many articles, surveys, and employee feedback, I realised what I really need to do first is to understand what it means for me personally. What can I contribute to a point of view for the team and the firm? I live in Melbourne with my wife and two children. Because of their ages, only my daughter is eligible for the vaccine. We have been isolated from our family abroad for more than two years now, and unfortunately don’t have a roadmap in sight on when we’ll see them next. We also have experienced a full 14-day home quarantine order, as the result of my (fully vaccinated) wife simply being at a grocery store that was later designated a Tier 1 exposure site. I am well aware this is not a unique story or even one that can be considered “doing it hard” in Victoria. But, it is my story and influences how I think about a return to office. Like so much of living through this pandemic, there are simply countless unknowns that make it incredibly difficult to plan ahead. What will our firm’s or landlord’s vaccination policy be? How will our local government regulate exposure sites? Will schools go back in session? What will my clients want from me and the team? As I wade through it all, it becomes apparent I am letting the environmental variables drive me – and this isn’t getting me anywhere. I determined I would consider what I want and who I am – irrespective of these variables. Before the pandemic, I most definitely was not a fan of working from home. I have never had a home office, and have always liked the routine of travelling to my different clients, teams, and offices. I really miss that in-person interaction. That said, I have discovered positives of working from home. I enjoy the quick afternoon walk at 3.30pm to pick my son up from school. I also enjoy the 15-minute morning drive to drop my teenage daughter off at school. This oftentimes is the only one-on-one time I get with her during the day. It is much more convenient to work right up to the very last minute on Thursday afternoons before I must leave to coach my son’s rugby team. This is much better than a stressful drive home through city traffic. Overall, I believe I am also more balanced in my personal life. And better integrated into my family life, as well. In the past it was much more difficult to manage all the different roles I play on a daily basis. Now, I will spend days in the office when we are able to do so. I will (happily!) get back on a plane to see clients in person as our country opens up. But, I will also continue to maintain my home office and integrate family responsibilities into my week. I believe many of my team members have also found similar new ways of managing their lives. Together, we will call upon our newfound flexibility and resilience, and simply adapt to whatever comes next. This is how we will lead and forge our way through this next phase. We will continue to adapt as needed. One small thing I have done off the back of all this change is to update my professional online persona to what it really looks like currently. The guy in the jacket posing in the office for a photo isn’t who I am right now and will not be the only professional me going forward. Jakob Dylan, said it best: Man, I ain't changed, but I know I ain't the same.

slides.title: My team supports each other to be flexible with ‘sacred days’
slides.subtitle: Kurt Solarte on LinkedIn
slides.description: Over the past couple of years, I have really found that flexibility (rather than the mythical 'work/life balance') is important to me, my health, and my family. In support of EY celebrating #EYFlextober, I sat down with our Talent team and had a chat about what flexibility means to me, and how my teams do #EYFlex This is that chat: Please tell us more about you, and about your role at EY. I am a Partner in EY Tech (Advisory) leading our teams around Digital and Emerging Technologies Why is flexibility important to you? Flexibility is important to me so that I can add ‘balance’ to my life, on my terms. Our work tends to peak and trough, and while my schedule is not always balanced, flexibility lets me make sure my life and my time with my family does balance out. How do you use flexibility/support you team to work flexibly? I like the idea of sacred days. Often technology projects can hit a frenzy of work, and we can lose focus of all things human. So, our teams often implement sacred days or times, where it is set aside, agreed by all, and each person gets that time to themselves, or family, or hobby. The teams really rally around each other to make those stay as sacred as possible. I personally set aside sacred time during rugby season, I play and coach rugby for the Melbourne Unicorns. This means I never travel on Thursdays, and I always leave work at 4:15 pm to make it to the pitch and setup for the boys. How have you dealt with difficult conversations with clients or with your team? I don’t actually believe these are difficult conversations. As it turns out, our clients are all humans and can relate to us when we show them we are human. I have the conversations with the senior client stakeholders early. I ensure them we will be staying on deadlines, giving them our all, and partnering with them to be successful; and for our team, being flexible is what that looks like. Most clients delivering large tech projects know they will come looking for extra work, a few late nights, and maybe even an occasional weekend, and so it is only fair that some flexibility throughout the project for our staff is granted. What tips would you give to other this #EYFlextober? Simply make it a priority. Like most things, if you put a bit of focus on it, it will happen. I know I feel healthier, happier, and more whole, when I have the flexibility to be who I really am. To find out more about flexibility @ EY, visit: https://www.ey.com/au/en/about-us/our-people-and-culture/ey-flexibility

Jacob is a graduate of Stevens Institute of Technology in Hoboken, NJ and Columbia Business School in New York, NY.

After a year and a half at Kerry, he moved to Dr. Oetker supervising the production of Ellio’s Pizza in Lodi, NJ. Dr. Oetker sold the Ellio's plant to be operated independently in April of 2021.

Jacob started the Executive MBA Program at Columbia Business School in the Fall of 2020 and graduated in May 2022. After Graduation he started at Ernst & Young as a Senior Consultant in their Supply Chain & Operations Practice.

Jacob is originally from Davis, California and decided to pursue his love of science and math by studying engineering at Stevens. 
In addition to his studies and his professional aspirations, Jacob has always tried to be involved in his community - from serving as the Mayor of the City of Davis for a day, to assisting with Hoboken's volunteering effort post-Hurricane Sandy. projects.title: ABE Fermentation - Nuts about Biofuel
projects.description: As dependence on fossil fuel becomes more and more prevalent and the unforeseen future of where overconsumption will lead, there becomes a need to explore alternative solutions such as biofuels. Acetone, butanol, and ethanol (ABE) have been produced by fermentation using a bacterial strain derived from starch and glucose to produce biofuels.  Alcohols, especially ethanol and butanol, have become target interest fuels because their chemical properties make them useful in internal combustion engines when blended with gasoline. ABE fermentation has the opportunity to become the economical and technological replacement for petrochemicals, especially when derived from renewable resources. The group investigated the reuse of starch-based packaging peanuts for this starch content to undergo ABE fermentation. The goal of this project is to simulate ABE fermentation on Aspen Plus V8.8 to develop the most economical conceptual design using starch.

publications.title: Using The Resource-Based View To Explore The Jamaican Health Tourism Sector As A Service: A Preliminary Examination
publications.description: Tourism plays a key role in the economy of the Caribbean Island of Jamaica, generating substantial revenues and contributing to employment. Jamaica endeavors to grow its economy and achieve developed nation status within the next two decades and is looking to tourism to help the country reach this goal. Specifically, Jamaica seeks to diversify its tourism offering by making a significant foray into what has been projected to be a highly lucrative health tourism market. While the potential for Jamaica to capitalize on the opportunities presented by this sector is substantial, much remains undiscovered about Jamaicas current position as well as what might be required to advance the nation in this area. The purpose of this paper is to provide a preliminary examination of Jamaicas health tourism sector within a resource-based view framework, highlighting the manner in which customers might serve as valuable resources and to examine a key element of the service delivery process.
